newsitem.title: USA: Babbitt says Headwaters, Yellowstone buy deal close.
newsitem.headline: Babbitt says Headwaters, Yellowstone buy deal close.

text.p: Interior Secretary Bruce Babbitt said Thursday that a deal with Congress to appropriate funds to save the Headwaters grove in California and a part of Yellowstone National Park was near completion.
"I'm confident that we are within striking distance of a deal," Babbitt told a National Press Club luncheon, despite the rejection of such funds by the House this week.

Babbitt said Congressional leaders made a deal with the administration to provide the funds when a balanced budget agreement was hammered out and that members of Congress are still committed to meeting their promise.

The House on Tuesday refused to use $700 million from a Land and Water Conservation fund to buy public lands, including $65 million to pay a company not to develop a gold mine on the edge of Yellowstone National Park, and $250 million to save the Headwaters grove in California, the nation's largest remaining uncut old-growth forest.

The White House has said the money must be provided in a final bill to meet its balanced budget with Congress. But Republicans said the money should not be used to buy new land when the government has trouble maintaining the land it has.
Babbitt also said a Senate bill to reauthorize the Endangered Species Act would probably be introduced before Congress adjourns in August for its summer recess.
"The Endangered Species Act is ripe for re-authorisation," Babbitt said. "We know what works and we know what doesn't."
Republican lawmakers last year launched an unsuccessful attempt to rewrite the Endangered Species Act to ease restrictions on developers and to improve the use of science in listing species.

Babbitt said reauthorization should not be used as a way to weaken the program's powers but to reform it to make it stronger. He suggested reforms could include the use of habit conservation planning programmes, activities to prevent species from becoming endangered and the involvement of states, tribes and local governments.
